extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, local/state/Tribal/Federal agencies, community officials, applicants, and other interested parties who would submit comments, appeals, or permit-related input to FEMA, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, or the U.S. International Trade Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments, appeals, and information in response to Federal Register notices (FEMA preliminary FIRMs/FIS, FWS recovery permit applications, and USITC complaints). Covers what content is useful, procedural requirements, deadlines, and filing formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Proposed Flood Hazard Determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA seeks general information and comment regarding the preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) and, where applicable, the Flood Insurance Study (FIS) report for listed communities; proposed determinations may include additions or modifications of any Base Flood Elevation (BFE), base flood depth, Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) boundary or zone designation, or regulatory floodway on the FIRM and FIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be submitted by the stated deadline (e.g., on or before August 20, 2025). Preliminary FIRM and FIS are available online (https://hazards.fema.gov/femaportal/prelimdownload) and at the listed Community Map Repository addresses; current effective FIRM/FIS are available at https://msc.fema.gov for comparison. Comments unrelated to the flood hazard determinations also will be considered before the FIRM/FIS become effective. The proposed determinations and the floodplain management criteria required by 44 CFR 60.3 are minimum requirements; communities may adopt stricter requirements. Contact and submission information (docket number, contact person, postal/email addresses, phone) is provided in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Requirements for Revised Flood Hazard Information (44 CFR 67.6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of revised flood hazard information shown on the Preliminary FIRM and FIS that satisfies the data requirements outlined in 44 CFR 67.6(b) is considered an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reconsideration must meet the data requirements in 44 CFR 67.6(b) to be treated as an appeal. Communities considering appeals should follow the procedural and data submission standards in that regulation. Use of a Scientific Resolution Panel (SRP) is available only after FEMA and local communities have engaged in collaborative consultation for at least 60 days without a mutually acceptable resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Resolution Panel (SRP) Use and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An SRP is an independent panel of experts in hydrology, hydraulics, and other pertinent sciences established to review conflicting scientific and technical data and provide recommendations for resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRP use may be exercised only after FEMA and the local community have engaged in collaborative consultation for at least 60 days without reaching a mutually acceptable resolution of an appeal. Additional SRP process information is available at https://www.floodsrp.org/pdfs/srp_overview.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability/Inspection of Preliminary and Effective Mapping Products
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary FIRM and FIS reports for each community are available for inspection online and at the respective Community Map Repository addresses; current effective FIRM and FIS reports are available through the FEMA Map Service Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect preliminary and effective maps to compare changes. For communities with multiple ongoing Preliminary studies, identify studies by unique project number and Preliminary FIRM date listed in the tables in the notice. Failure to inspect available materials does not remove procedural requirements for comments/appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: FWS Invitation to Comment on Recovery Permit Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service invites local, State, Tribal, and Federal agencies and the public to review and comment on applications received for recovery permits under section 10(a)(1)(A) of the Endangered Species Act prior to issuance of permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be received by the deadline (e.g., on or before June 23, 2025). Requests and comments should specify the applicant’s name and application number (e.g., PER0001234). Documents and application materials are available for review subject to the Privacy Act and FOIA. Contact information (email, mailing address, phone) for regional permit staff is provided in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content That Is Most Useful for FWS Permit Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments and recommendations that are supported by quantitative information or studies are the most useful and most likely to influence agency decisions regarding recovery permit applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, supply quantitative data, study results, or citations to peer-reviewed or technical reports. Describe methods, geographic/temporal scope, and relevance to the permit's proposed activities (e.g., capture, handling, monitoring, translocation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to Include in FWS Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests and comments should specify the applicant’s name and application number and may include written data, views, or arguments with respect to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear identification (applicant name and PER number), supporting data or studies, and contact information if desired. Be aware comments become part of the administrative record and may be disclosed under FOIA/Privacy Act constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Availability of Comments and Privacy Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments become part of the administrative record and may be made publicly available; personal identifying information included in comments may be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include your address, phone number, email, or other personal identifying information, it may be publicly available. You may request withholding of personal identifying information, but the agency cannot guarantee it can honor that request. Submissions from organizations or individuals identifying as organization representatives will be disclosed in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Authority and Applicable Permit Regulations (FWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recovery permits under section 10(a)(1)(A) of the ESA are governed by the ESA and implementing regulations at 50 CFR part 17 (e.g., 17.22, 17.32, 17.62, 17.72 as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit applicants and commenters should reference the applicable regulatory sections for endangered vs. threatened, plant vs. wildlife species to understand statutory/regulatory standards for permit issuance and permitted activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Interest Factors to Address in USITC Section 337 Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission solicits comments addressing whether issuance of requested remedial relief (e.g., limited exclusion orders, cease and desist orders) would affect public health and welfare, competitive conditions in the U.S. economy, domestic production of like or directly competitive articles, or U.S. consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, the Commission is interested in comments that: (i) explain how the articles potentially subject to remedial orders are used in the U.S.; (ii) identify public health, safety, or welfare concerns related to the requested remedial orders; (iii) identify like or directly competitive articles made in the U.S. that could replace the subject articles if excluded; (iv) indicate whether complainant/licensees/third-party suppliers have capacity to replace the volume within a commercially reasonable time; and (v) explain how the requested remedial orders would impact U.S. consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Deadlines, Page Limits, and Filing Rules (USITC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written submissions on the public interest must be filed by the close of business eight calendar days after publication of the notice in the Federal Register; replies by complainant may be filed no later than three calendar days after initial submissions were due; other submissions must meet the same eight-day deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions and replies are limited to five (5) pages inclusive of attachments. Persons must file the original document electronically by the deadlines via the Commission’s Electronic Document Information System (EDIS) at https://edis.usitc.gov. Include the docket number prominently (e.g., 'Docket No. 3830'). The Secretary's Office will accept only electronic filings during this time; no in-person paper filings or paper copies of electronic filings will be accepted until further notice. Questions about filing should be sent to EDIS3Help@usitc.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Limits on Submissions (USITC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only submissions specifically requested in the notice or otherwise permitted by the Commission will be accepted; no other submissions will be accepted unless requested by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the notice for the topics and timing for submissions. Complainant may file replies within the specified three-day window. Ensure any submission complies with the page limit and filing system requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and Participation in Administrative Proceedings (General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices list who may participate (e.g., any persons who requested opportunity to participate at hearings) and provide guidance on how interested parties can access public versions of documents (e.g., EDIs for USITC, FOIA/Privacy Act review for FWS, FEMA portals for maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties should consult the notice for how to access public records (EDIS, FEMA portals, regional offices), deadlines for participation, and contact points for further information. Hearing-impaired persons are given TTY/TDD/relay instructions where applicable.
